title: Hai-Anh H. Dang | Senior Economist, Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS), World Bank
gist: A World Bank staff-profile page for LSMS Senior Economist Hai-Anh H. Dang, whose methodological specialty in constructing synthetic panel data from cross-sectional surveys underpins a July 2026 post on measuring multidimensional poverty in countries with incomplete data.

insights.claim: Dang's methodological specialty is constructing 'synthetic (pseudo) panel data from cross sections' — a technique enabling estimation of poverty and welfare dynamics in countries that lack true longitudinal household panel surveys.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A named, reusable methodology for tracking poverty trends in countries without panel data — relevant for assessing data reliability behind World Bank poverty statistics in low-capacity statistical systems.
insights.locator: methodology to construct synthetic (pseudo) panel data from cross sections

insights.claim: His most recent listed post, 'Measuring multidimensional poverty in countries with incomplete data' (July 23, 2026), applies this cross-survey/incomplete-data methodology focus to multidimensional poverty measurement, continuing a research line stretching back to 2014 on tracking poverty without full panel data.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Flags a current (mid-2026) World Bank methodological push on multidimensional poverty measurement for countries with data gaps — relevant for interpreting the reliability of newly published poverty figures from low-capacity statistical systems.
insights.locator: Measuring multidimensional poverty in countries with incomplete data, July 23, 2026

insights.claim: Dang has also worked on measuring poverty among refugees specifically through cross-survey imputation methods designed to substitute for data scarcity in forced-displacement contexts.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Names a specific applied use case (refugee poverty measurement via imputation) relevant to humanitarian-data and forced-displacement analysis.
insights.locator: Measuring poverty of refugees: Can cross-survey imputation methods substitute for data scarcity?
